subject: geography
topicDisplay: Earths Life Support Systems Water Carbon Cycles
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Combustion of fossil fuels transfers carbon from which store to which store?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon stored in geological deposits into the atmosphere as CO2.

questions.q: Cloud feedback is uncertain in climate science because clouds can:
options: Both reflect incoming sunlight (cooling) and trap outgoing heat (warming)
questions.explain: Clouds exert both a cooling (albedo) and a warming (greenhouse) effect, making their net feedback hard to predict.

questions.q: Land-use change such as deforestation affects the carbon cycle primarily by:
options: Permanently removing carbon to sedimentary rock
Increasing the size of the terrestrial biomass store
Reducing photosynthetic uptake and releasing stored carbon
questions.explain: Clearing forest cuts carbon sequestration and, when biomass decomposes or burns, releases CO2 to the atmosphere.

questions.q: A biome is best described as:
options: A large-scale community of plants and animals adapted to a particular climate
A single population of one species
questions.explain: A biome is a global-scale ecosystem type defined by its climate and characteristic vegetation and fauna.

questions.q: The terrestrial carbon store fluctuates seasonally mainly because:
options: Northern-hemisphere photosynthesis draws down CO2 in the growing season
Ocean currents reverse twice a year
Fossil-fuel use is highest in spring
questions.explain: During the northern growing season, vegetation photosynthesis lowers atmospheric CO2, producing the seasonal sawtooth.

questions.q: Energy enters most ecosystems and flows in which direction?
options: It is recycled endlessly like nutrients
It flows one way from the Sun through trophic levels and is lost as heat
It flows from consumers to producers
questions.explain: Unlike nutrients, energy flows unidirectionally from sunlight through producers and consumers and is ultimately lost as heat.

questions.q: Net primary productivity (NPP) is calculated as:
questions.explain: NPP is gross primary productivity minus the energy lost through plant respiration, i.e. the energy available to consumers.

questions.q: A complete sequence of seral stages in a particular succession is called a:
questions.explain: A sere is the full set of seral stages from pioneer community to climax.

questions.q: In savanna grasslands, periodic fire acts as:
options: An arresting factor that maintains grassland by limiting tree growth
A nutrient sink that removes all minerals permanently
questions.explain: Regular fires suppress tree saplings and recycle nutrients, helping maintain the grassland as a fire (plagio)climax.

questions.q: UK heather moorland maintained by regular burning and sheep grazing is an example of a:
questions.explain: Heather moorland is a plagioclimax kept in place by management practices that prevent woodland regeneration.

questions.q: An arresting factor in succession is one that:
options: Halts or deflects succession, preventing the climatic climax
questions.explain: Arresting factors, such as grazing, fire or trampling, stop succession reaching its natural climax.

questions.q: The fast carbon cycle is best characterised by:
options: Carbon stored permanently in fossil fuels
Carbon movement only between the two polar ice sheets
Carbon exchange over millions of years via rock weathering and burial
Rapid exchange of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, vegetation and soils over years to centuries
questions.explain: The fast carbon cycle moves carbon relatively quickly between the atmosphere, biosphere, soils and surface ocean.

questions.q: Which strategy best combines ecological and economic sustainability in rainforest management?
options: Ecotourism and agroforestry that generate income while conserving the forest
Total exclusion of all human use
questions.explain: Ecotourism and agroforestry provide livelihoods while keeping the forest largely intact, balancing conservation with development.

questions.q: Why does increased atmospheric CO2 represent a disruption to the natural carbon budget?
options: Anthropogenic emissions exceed the rate at which natural sinks can absorb them
It is fully offset by silicate weathering within months
Vegetation growth removes it within one season
The oceans instantly absorb all additional CO2
questions.explain: Human emissions outpace the uptake capacity of land and ocean sinks, so atmospheric CO2 accumulates.

questions.q: A succession that develops on bare rock is specifically termed a:
questions.explain: A lithosere is the succession beginning on a bare rock surface.

questions.q: Biodiversity is best defined as:
options: The number of trophic levels only
The variety of species, genetic and habitat diversity within an area
questions.explain: Biodiversity encompasses species, genetic and ecosystem/habitat variety.

questions.q: On a storm hydrograph, a short lag time and high peak discharge are most associated with:
options: A basin with deep groundwater storage
An impermeable, urbanised or saturated basin
A basin during a prolonged drought
questions.explain: Low infiltration and rapid overland flow in impermeable or saturated basins produce a flashy hydrograph.

questions.q: Decomposers (detritivores and saprotrophs) are essential to ecosystems because they:
options: Break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients into the soil store
questions.explain: Decomposers release nutrients locked in dead matter back into the soil, sustaining the nutrient cycle.

questions.q: Primary succession differs from secondary succession because primary succession:
options: Begins on a previously vegetated surface after disturbance
Begins on a newly exposed surface with no pre-existing soil or seed bank
questions.explain: Primary succession starts on bare, lifeless surfaces (e.g. bare rock, new lava) lacking soil, whereas secondary succession follows disturbance of an already-soiled area.

questions.q: Carbon flux from vegetation to the atmosphere occurs mainly through:
questions.explain: Respiration by plants and decomposition of organic matter return CO2 from the biosphere to the atmosphere.

questions.q: During a prolonged summer in a temperate basin, the water balance typically shows:
options: A soil-moisture deficit and utilisation of stored water
questions.explain: In summer potential evapotranspiration exceeds precipitation, drawing on stored soil water and creating a moisture deficit.

questions.q: Deforestation in a tropical drainage basin most directly alters the water cycle by:
options: Reducing evapotranspiration and increasing surface runoff
questions.explain: Removing trees lowers interception and transpiration while increasing overland flow and flood risk.

questions.q: Which process transfers water directly from a solid or liquid surface store to the atmospheric store without involving plants?
questions.explain: Evaporation converts liquid water to vapour directly from surfaces, while transpiration involves vegetation.

questions.q: The climatic climax community is the:
options: Stable end-point community in equilibrium with the regional climate
questions.explain: The climatic climax is the self-sustaining community in equilibrium with the prevailing climate.

questions.q: A glacier melting in response to warming, exposing darker rock that absorbs more heat, is an example of:
questions.explain: Reduced ice cover lowers albedo, increasing heat absorption and further melting, a positive feedback.

questions.q: Selective logging is considered more sustainable than clear-felling because it:
options: Takes only certain trees, allowing forest structure and regeneration to remain
questions.explain: Removing only selected mature trees maintains canopy and soil structure, allowing the forest to regenerate.

questions.q: In the Gersmehl nutrient-cycling model, the three stores of nutrients are:
questions.explain: Gersmehl represents nutrient cycling between three stores: biomass, litter and soil.

questions.q: A water budget graph for a location shows recharge occurring when:
options: Soil-moisture deficit is at a maximum
Precipitation exceeds potential evapotranspiration and the soil refills
questions.explain: Recharge happens when precipitation surplus replenishes depleted soil-moisture stores.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, gross primary productivity (GPP) refers to:
options: Energy lost at each trophic transfer
The total rate at which producers fix energy through photosynthesis
questions.explain: GPP is the total rate of energy capture by autotrophs before any is used in respiration.

questions.q: Which statement about the link between the water and carbon cycles is correct?
options: The carbon cycle has no influence on climate
Water has no role in carbon transfer
They operate entirely independently of each other
Vegetation links them by both transpiring water and fixing carbon
questions.explain: Plants couple the cycles: photosynthesis fixes carbon while transpiration moves water, and both respond to climate.
